newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - March4.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest - March4.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Poland's Economic Competition Office imposed a one-million-forint ($5,650) fine on Polgari Bank and issued a formal reprimand for an advertisement containing misleading information. The fine followed an investigation after a consumer said a bank ad for a 4-month investment vehicle which promised 28 percent annual interest was misleading. (Figyelo, February 20, 1997)

-- The Czech Advertising Council rejected a proposal to expand the ethic code to cover two new areas. The proposal would have stopped ad agencies from publishing so-called undignified portrayals of male and female bodies and would have banned automobile ads from focussing on fast driving. (Mlada Fronta Dnes, February 28, 1997).
-- The advertising agency Publicis FCB Praha has won a new
client in the Czech Republic -- the French giant Besnier International, which makes camembert, brie and other cheese. (Strategie, February 19-26, 1997)

-- Bates/Saatchi & Saatch have sent out flyers to small- and medium-sized companies in the Czech Republic for the "Business Software Alliance" to raise awareness about computer software piracy. (Strategie, February 19-26, 1997)

-- Budapest will host an international sports marketing conference in mid-March 1997, which, with the help of European experts, aims to promote a more cooperation between sports and marketing. (Vilaggazdasag, February 27, 1997)

-- Only two percent of Polish-based companies' advertising budgets is spent on direct mail, which makes the country one of Europe's least developed direct mail markets, according to a report by Artur D. Little Poland consulting. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)

-- A new survey in the Czech Republic indicates young people are increasingly aware of brand names. The study by GfK Praha market research institute covered 2,000 people aged 14 to 24. Fifty-four percent said brand names guaranteed quality, while 72 percent said they did not always buy the same brand. Brand-name products were virtually non-existent in the Czech Republic before 1989. (Ekonom, February 27 - March 5, 1997)

-- Hungary's four leading tobacco firms appear to have agreed on the wording of a self-regulatory ethics code aimed at complementing regulations on tobacco advertising that will be included in a new advertising law. The new law, which is expected to pass by Parliament by mid-March, will be in line with legislation in the OECD countries. (Vilaggazdasag, February 27, 1997)

-- Flora vegetable fat says a telephone information service that it set up for Czech consumers has logged 500 calls from shoppers interested in cholesterol, combatting fat and other nutrition issues. Eight percent of the callers were women. (Pravo, February 25, 1997)

-- Uroda SA cosmetics maker and Cussons Poland, both controlled by Cussons International, have started an advertising campaign in Poland for Multident toothpaste which will last till May 1997. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)

MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:-- The film "Dances with Wolves" was the most watched film on Czech television in 1996, with 70 percent of viewers recently surveyed having seen it. The most watched programme on Ceska Televise was the European football championship. (Lidove Noviny, February 26, 1997)

-- The Czech television stations Ceska Televize and TV Nova say they are interested in broadcasting top Czech football leagues live, in case FilmNet Channel is unable to broadcast football. According to earlier reports, FilmNet will end its broadcasting in March in Central Europe and will unable to fulfill its contract with the Czech-Moravian football league for exclusive television rights. (Pravo, February 26, 1997)

-- A new software programme by Cabria Software and Seznam in the Czech Republic offers Internet users income tax information services and copies of Czech laws and regulations. The service is part of a business information service package called Cabria WebOffice, located at www.cabria.cz on the Internet. (Pravo, February 25, 1997)

-- The film "People versus Larry Flynt" by the Czech director Milos Forman premiered in Prague on February 22. It was promoted by Falcon and Grundig and Oasa Studio advertising agency. (Tyden, February 24, 1997)

-- The first channel of the Hungarian Television (MTV) and the North American television series Emergency had the largest television audience in late January and early February. Hungarian Television earns 21 million forints in gross revenue for a five-minute commercial slot before the top hit series. (Vilaggazdasag, February 27, 1997)
-- A new business radio broadcasting network, Goldnet, has begun operations in the Czech Republic. (Pravo, February 26, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:

-- The general director of Toyota Motor Czech, Jaromir Stribrny, says Toyota will be more active, visible and diversified in the Czech Republic this year. Toyota recently introduced locally its luxury Camry and is one of the sponsors of an up-coming concert in Prague by Phil Collins. Toyota says its goal is to sell 3,300 vehicles in the Czech Republic this year. (Tyden, February 24, 1997)

-- The listed Okocim brewery will start production of Carlsberg beer on a licence granted by Okocim's parent company, Denmark's Carlsberg A.S. The new beer brand will be marketed only in Poland. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)

-- Raisio Polska Foods, a branch of Finland's margarine concern, will introduce a new "economy margarine" at 1.09 zlotys (35 cents) per 250 gramme pack in February. There is a big demand for economically priced fat products, says Raisio brand manager Miroslaw Janicki. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)

-- Amway Poland network marketing firm's sales reached 160 million zlotys ($52.3 million) in 1996, which was Europe's third biggest turnover, Amway Poland general director Marek Florczuk said. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)
CONSUMER TRENDS:
-- Polish teenagers are spending between 1.9 and 2.3 million zlotys a year, the Getas IRWiK research institute director Anna Olejniczuk said. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)

-- An average Pole spends about 34 zlotys annually on cosmetics products, including perfume and deodorant -- which is one-tenth the amount spent in France. But Poles are becoming more selective about the products they buy, according to research by the MEMRB market monitoring agency. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)
-- Winiary food company says food surveys show Poles are increasingly keen on Italian cooking sauces. Winiary is a subsidiary of Nestle's. (Marketing Polska, February 1997)
